$comment: The case DSL definition (RFC 0001 §4.3). A primitive exists iff this schema admits it. additionalProperties:false at every level — the schema refuses what it does not name.

$schema.$comment: optional editor association; ignored by the gate
$schema.description: Optional editor association; ignored by the gate.

id.description: CASE-<kebab-slug>, unique across the set. Compiled cases end in a 3-digit ordinal (CASE-order-create-001).

title.description: Optional human title — usually the acceptance-criterion sentence this case verifies.

notes.description: Optional free text for reviewers. Never interpreted.

from.$comment: template/seed/instance appear only on cases minted from an invariant template at run time

intent.description: The intent section id this case was compiled from (the `id=` in the section's tag, or the slug derived from its heading).

hash.description: Content-hash prefix of the live section text. Mechanical — never written by hand or by the model; run `peira stamp` to fill it.

template.description: Only on cases minted at run time from an invariant template: the TPL- id.

seed.description: Only on minted cases: the run seed. (template, seed, instance) regenerates the case bit-for-bit.

instance.description: Only on minted cases: the instance index within the run.

from.description: Lineage: which intent section, at which content hash, produced this case. `intent` is authored by a human; `hash` is never authored — compile stamps it, and `peira stamp` fills or refreshes it for hand-written cases. A hash that no longer matches the live section marks the case stale; a missing hash marks it unstamped.

setup.description: Optional steps run in order before `test`: request steps, or invocations of registry steps (procedure only — an invocation cannot carry expect or capture).

test.description: Exactly one request step. The claim under test lives in its `expect`.

teardown.description: Optional {"drain": true}: after the verdict, the runner polls every id this case captured — via the bed's `drain` probe, under the credentials that captured it — until each reaches a terminal state. Replaces sleep-and-pray cleanup.

invocation.$comment: A step invocation (RFC §4.5): procedure only, setup only. It structurally cannot carry expect or capture — the claim being verified stays in the case's declarative test.

step.description: The registry step to invoke: STEP-<kebab-slug>.

bind.description: Values for the step's declared `reads`, by name. Values interpolate like any request value.

request.description: The HTTP request this step issues.

capture.$comment: free map: alias -> response path; keys and values are checked statically in validate.js
capture.description: alias → dotted response path rooted at status, body, or headers (body.id, headers.location). Later steps reference the value as "$alias" (whole value, type-preserving) or "{{alias}}" inside a string. A path missing from the response fails the case, naming the path.

until.description: The expect block that ends the polling when it matches.

timeoutMs.description: Ceiling in milliseconds; hitting it is a fail (the predicate never held), not an error.

pollUntil.description: Re-issue this step's request until `until` (an expect block) matches — at a pinned 100 ms interval, up to `timeoutMs` (default 10 s, or the bed's timeouts.pollUntilMs). Non-convergence is a fail. The declarative replacement for wall-clock sleeps, which are refused.

expect.description: The oracle for this step. Subset matching with Jest toMatchObject parity: objects as subsets at every level, arrays index-wise with equal length, primitives strictly.

route.description: Path starting with /. Inside a route use {{alias}} to splice a captured value — a bare $alias is only meaningful as a whole value and is literal text inside a longer string (validate warns).

query.description: Optional object → query string. Values may be "$alias" or contain {{alias}}.

body.description: Optional JSON body, sent as application/json; skipped for get. Any value may reference captures or {{unique.<key>}}.

anyOf.description: A bed principal by alias. Legal only here, never spliced into data.

username.description: Literal username — negative Basic tests only.

password.description: Literal password — negative Basic tests only (redacted from the evidence log by key).

anyOf.description: Literal Basic credentials — for negative auth tests; real principals live in the bed.

token.description: The token value to send (scrubbed from the evidence log by value).

header.description: Header name to carry the token, e.g. Authorization or X-API-Key.

format.description: Header value template; must contain {{token}}, e.g. "Bearer {{token}}".

send.description: How to attach it: {header, format containing {{token}}} or {cookie}.

anyOf.description: Literal token — for negative token tests. `send` optional: defaults to {header: Authorization, format: "Bearer {{token}}"}.

auth.description: Four forms: "$users.<alias>" (a bed principal — Basic, login, or static token; the bed decides), a literal {username, password} (negative Basic-auth tests), a literal {token, send?} (negative token tests; defaults to Authorization: Bearer), or absent for anonymous. Never invent principals.

followRedirects.description: Default true. false makes the step see its own 3xx, so expect.status 307 and expect.headers.location are assertable and capture: {"next": "headers.location"} is meaningful.

headers.$comment: response-header assertions; names are matched case-insensitively. Free map: name -> literal string | matcher; value shapes are checked statically in validate.js
headers.description: Response headers by name, case-insensitive. Each value is a literal string or a matcher ($any, $contains, $notContains, $absent); anything else is refused statically. A missing header is a named diff. Repeated headers arrive joined with ", " (Set-Cookie included), so $contains matches any one of them.

body.description: Subset match against the response body. JSON bodies are parsed; any other body is a string, and $contains / $notContains are the oracle for it. Matchers: {"$any": "string"|"number"|"boolean"}, {"$contains": "s" | ["s", ...]} (all of), {"$notContains": "s" | ["s", ...]} (none of), {"$absent": true} (key must not exist), and literal null (present and null). Matchers stand alone.

bodySchema.description: A JSON-Schema subset the whole body must satisfy — type, required, properties, additionalProperties, enum, items, pattern, anyOf — for "every element has shape X" claims. Use expect.body for concrete values.
